sentence: This project runs sequencing on nasal, blood and sputum samples to study single cell gene expression and immune receptors in respiratory viral infections.
This project studies the structure and function of an enzyme and tetraspanin protein complex to see how the protein affects which substrates the enzyme targets.
This project uses tools from systems biology to understand how tumors and the immune system interact and to find ways to improve cancer immunotherapy responses.
This project studies how respiratory exposures from Gulf War deployment lead to lung cancer, using lung specimens from veterans and mice exposed to toxins.
This project studies postmortem brain tissue and basal ganglia organoids to find out how Tourette syndrome develops.
This project builds a method that uses enzymatic conversions to map an epigenetic modification of DNA in damaged clinical samples to detect cancer signatures.
This project studies how abundant gut bacteria get nutrients and resist antimicrobials.
This project uses large-scale recording to study how the hippocampus and entorhinal cortex form memories of spatial reward.
This project studies how interferon gamma sets up memory in different types of innate immune cells.
This project develops methods based on genomics to track how infections spread in hospitals.
This project studies how an understudied protein linked to a rare disease works in endocytosis in live cells and during neuronal development.
This project builds a tool that reads RNA and protein in place to show how bacteria and their host tissue interact.
This project studies how neural progenitors produce oligodendrocyte lineage cells, which wrap axons with insulating myelin.
This project studies how cells change fate at different times during bone fracture healing to make tissues that heal the injured bone.
This project uses mice to study how the medial prefrontal cortex develops and changes across life stages.
This project studies the role of one molecule in pancreatic beta cells to understand what drives Type 2 diabetes.
This project studies how breast cancer cells release a glycosylated protein that opens the blood-brain barrier so cancer spreads to the brain.
This project tests whether diffusion magnetic resonance imaging can detect changes in synaptic density in Alzheimer's disease.
This project studies how two enzymes that edit DNA and RNA push blood stem cells to become leukemia stem cells in myeloproliferative neoplasms.
This project builds ways to train artificial intelligence models on diabetes data from many sites without sharing sensitive patient information.
